title: Frequent Itemsets & Association Rules
interviewAnswer: Association-rule mining finds frequent item combinations and rules A→B. Support measures frequency, confidence estimates P(B|A), and lift compares the rule with B’s baseline rate.
why: This is a classic data-mining pattern for market baskets and co-occurrence.
intuition: Bread and butter appearing together is only interesting if the co-occurrence is frequent and stronger than what item popularity alone predicts.
deepDive: Apriori uses downward closure: if an itemset is frequent, its subsets must be frequent, which prunes the exponential search.
production: Control combinatorial explosion and validate discovered rules with domain context.
workedExample: A rule can have high confidence because B is common; lift reveals whether A truly adds association.
